findings.title: AI agent can read tenant data and send it out (exfiltration path)
findings.description: AI agent 'Finance Copilot Agent' combines broad read access (Files.Read.All, Mail.Read) with an egress channel (Mail.Send): the 'lethal trifecta' of private data, untrusted input and external communication.
findings.attack_path_context: Indirect prompt injection: an attacker emails or shares a document containing instructions; the agent reads it, collects data via Files.Read.All and exfiltrates it via Mail.Send — no credential theft required.

findings.title: Credentials added to a Microsoft first-party service principal
findings.description: Service principal 'Office 365 Exchange Online' has 1 credential(s) set on the service principal object itself. These do not appear under 'Certificates & secrets' in the portal and are a well-known persistence technique (Solorigate / Midnight Blizzard).
findings.attack_path_context: An attacker with Application.ReadWrite.All or Application Administrator can silently add a secret here and authenticate as this identity indefinitely. Whoever holds it inherits every permission granted to the identity.
findings.remediation_cli:
# Check who added them (Entra audit log: 'Add service principal credentials'), then delete what nobody recognises:

findings.title: Dormant for 240 days with 1 valid credential(s)
findings.description: 'legacy-hr-sync' last authenticated 240 days ago but still holds 1 valid credential(s). Nobody would notice if it started signing in again.
findings.attack_path_context: Dormant identities with live credentials are prime targets: their activity is not baselined, so an attacker using a leaked secret blends in. Whoever holds it inherits Graph Directory.ReadWrite.All; directory role(s) User Administrator — a direct privilege-escalation path.
findings.remediation_cli:
# 1. Disable the identity. This is reversible: set accountEnabled=true to undo it.
az ad sp update --id 59cf3713-48f3-5dce-8d5e-97c546a0e41f --set accountEnabled=false
# 2. After an observation period with no impact, remove its credentials:
# az ad app credential delete --id eb1e81d4-3c80-5f0b-bbf5-b20d1eebbd45 --key-id 963474b3-2d0d-587c-9259-420036e153b1

findings.title: Contributor on 1 subscription-level scope(s)
findings.description: 'ci-deploy-pipeline' is Contributor at subscription or management-group scope. Pipelines rarely need more than a few resource groups.
findings.attack_path_context: Contributor can deploy and modify any resource: run code on VMs and Automation accounts, read storage keys, and attach privileged managed identities to attacker-controlled resources.
findings.remediation_cli:
# 1. Grant Contributor only where it is needed (repeat for each resource group):
az role assignment create --assignee 721f86b6-720c-5b98-9376-f38c527dee54 --role Contributor --scope "<RESOURCE_GROUP_SCOPE>"
# 2. Confirm the workload still runs, then remove the broad assignment:

findings.title: Client secret valid for 730 days
findings.description: 'ci-deploy-pipeline' has 1 active client secret(s) with a lifetime above 365 days (longest: 730 days). Long-lived static secrets end up in config files, CI variables and chat history.
findings.attack_path_context: A leaked long-lived secret stays valid for months without anyone noticing. Whoever holds it inherits Azure Contributor on subscription, User Access Administrator on resource group — a direct privilege-escalation path.
findings.remediation_cli:
# 1. Add a federated credential for the workload. Adapt issuer and subject (GitHub Actions example):
# az ad app federated-credential create --id 721f86b6-720c-5b98-9376-f38c527dee54 --parameters '{"name":"github-main","issuer":"https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com","subject":"repo:<ORG>/<REPO>:ref:refs/heads/main","audiences":["api://AzureADTokenExchange"]}'
# 2. Switch the workload to it and confirm it signs in.
# 3. Only then delete the old secret(s):
# az ad app credential delete --id 721f86b6-720c-5b98-9376-f38c527dee54 --key-id d12787a1-899f-5adf-abe1-7d48511537f4

findings.title: All credentials expire within 11 days
findings.description: Every valid credential of 'marketing-analytics-poc' expires within 30 days and no replacement exists yet. Unplanned expiry causes outages and rushed, insecure rotations.
findings.attack_path_context: Emergency rotations are when secrets get pasted into tickets and chats, or issued with multi-year lifetimes 'to avoid this next time'.
findings.remediation_cli:
# 1. Add a federated credential for the workload. Adapt issuer and subject (GitHub Actions example):
# az ad app federated-credential create --id f82dda04-e8f5-5cea-91b4-5da750927a8c --parameters '{"name":"github-main","issuer":"https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com","subject":"repo:<ORG>/<REPO>:ref:refs/heads/main","audiences":["api://AzureADTokenExchange"]}'
# 2. Switch the workload to it and confirm it signs in.
# or, if a new secret is unavoidable, store it in Key Vault so it never reaches the terminal:
# az keyvault secret set --vault-name "<VAULT_NAME>" --name rotated-f82dda04-e8f5-5cea-91b4-5da750927a8c -o none --value "$(az ad app credential reset --id f82dda04-e8f5-5cea-91b4-5da750927a8c --append --display-name rotated --end-date 2027-04-28 --query password -o tsv)"
